'''Hubert Saleur''' (born December 28, 1960 in [[Aix-en-Provence]], France) is a French-American [[theoretical physicist]].<ref name="website">{{Cite web |title=Home {{!}} Hubert Saleur |url=https://hsaleur.org/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=hsaleur.org}}</ref> He has worked on [[quantum field theories]] and their applications to [[condensed matter physics]] and [[statistical mechanics]].<ref name="USCtoday">{{Cite web |title=Hubert Saleur |url=https://today.usc.edu/profile/hubert-saleur/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=USC Today |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Packard">{{Cite web |title=Saleur, Hubert M. • The David and Lucile Packard Foundation |url=https://www.packard.org/fellow/saleur-hubert-m/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=The David and Lucile Packard Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> He has received recognition from the [[French Physical Society]] for his contributions to the study of [[phase transitions]] in disordered quantum systems and transport problems in [[nanophysics]],<ref name="FPS">{{Cite web |date=2019-09-12 |title=Hubert Saleur, lauréat du Prix Jean Ricard 2018 |url=https://www.sfphysique.fr/hubert-saleur-laureat-du-prix-jean-ricard-2018/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=Société Française de Physique |language=fr-FR}}</ref> and by the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]] for his contributions to [[conformal field theory]].<ref name="CNRS">[https://www.cnrs.fr/sites/default/files/download-file/SaleurH.pdf CNRS silver medalist profile (pdf, in French)]</ref> His work includes the exact determination of [[critical exponents]] in two-dimensional [[percolation]].<ref name="FPS" />

== Education ==

Saleur was a student at [[École Normale Supérieure de Lyon]] (formerly St Cloud) from 1981 to 1985, and earned a Ph.D. in physics from [[Université Paris 6]] in 1987.<ref name="website" />

== Career ==

From 1986 to 1990, Saleur worked as a CNRS research associate at Service de Physique Théorique (Saclay, France) (currently [[Institute of Theoretical Physics, Saclay]]). From 1991 to 1992 he worked at [[Yale University]], first as an assistant professor and then as an associate professor.
He has been affiliated with [[University of Southern California]] (USC) since 1993, first as an associate professor and later, since 1996, as professor of physics and mathematics (currently on leave). He has also been a member of the [[Caltech]] - USC Center for Theoretical Physics between 1999 and 2002, and has been an international director of research at the [[Institute of Theoretical Physics, Saclay]] since 2004.<ref name="website" /><ref name="IPhT_staff">{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Mathematical physics, string theory and gravity - IPhT |url=https://www.ipht.fr/en/mathematical-physics-string-theory-and-gravity/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=www.ipht.fr |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="USC">[https://dornsife.usc.edu/profile/hubert-saleur/ USC Dornsife]</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

* 1987 – ''Doisteau Blutel Prize'' of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] (with [[Bertrand Duplantier]]) <ref name="USC"/>
* 1987 – Bronze Medal of the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]].<ref name="USC"/>
* 1991 – David and Lucile Packard Fellowship <ref name="Packard" />
* 1993 – National Young Investigator Award, [[U.S. National Science Foundation]]<ref name="USC"/>
* 2001 – Humboldt Senior Research Award (Germany)<ref name="USC"/>
* 2011 – Silver Medal of the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]]<ref name="CNRS" />
* 2015 – Advanced Research Grant, [[European Research Council]] (ERC)<ref name="IPhT_ERC">{{Cite web |last=NONNENMACHER |first=Stephane |date=2015-06-22 |title=Hubert Saleur receives an ERC Advanced Grant - IPhT |url=https://www.ipht.fr/en/2015/06/hubert-saleur-receives-an-erc-advanced-grant/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=www.ipht.fr |language=en-GB}}</ref>
* 2019 – Jean Ricard Grand Prize of the [[French Physical Society]]<ref name="FPS"/><ref name="USC"/>
* 2025 – [[Ampère Prize]]<ref name="IPhT_news">{{Cite web |access-date=2026-05-18 |title=Hubert Saleur wins the 2025 Ampère Grand Prize of the French Academy of Sciences. |url=https://www.ipht.fr/en/2025/10/hubert-saleur-receives-the-ampere-prize/  |website=www.ipht.fr |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="French_academy">{{Cite web |access-date=2026-05-18 |title=Press release of the French Academy of Sciences. |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/communique-de-presse-premiere-seance-solennelle-de-remise-des-prix-de-lacademie-des-sciences-28  |website= www.academie-sciences.fr/ |language=fr}}</ref>



== Selected publications ==

* V. Pasquier & H. Saleur (1990), ''Common structures between finite systems and conformal field theories through quantum groups'', Nuclear Physics B 330 (2-3), 523–556
* H. Saleur & B. Duplantier (1987), ''Exact determination of the percolation hull exponent in two dimensions'', Physical Review Letters 58 (22), 2325
* B. Duplantier & H. Saleur (1987), ''Exact tricritical exponents for polymers at the Θ-point in two dimensions'', Physical Review Letters 59 (5), 539
* P. Fendley, A. W. W. Ludwig & H. Saleur (1995), ''Exact conductance through point contacts in the ν = 1/3 fractional quantum Hall effect'', Physical Review Letters 74 (15), 3005
* P. Fendley, A. W. W. Ludwig & H. Saleur (1995), ''Exact nonequilibrium transport through point contacts in quantum wires and fractional quantum Hall devices'', Physical Review B 52 (12), 8934
